The fork's first minor release: Pulumi and the providers updated, Astro 6 and 7, and fixes for `sst dev` and deploys. Still built on upstream [v4.17.1](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/releases/tag/v4.17.1).

### ⚠️ Breaking changes

All from the Pulumi and provider update ([#18](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/18)):

- **Node.js 22 or later is required.** Pulumi's Node.js SDK, which runs your `sst.config.ts`, needs it. On an older Node.js the CLI warns that SST needs Node.js 22 or later. Node.js 20 mostly works, but inline Lambda callbacks fail. Upgrade Node.js everywhere you run `sst`, CI included.
- **A deploy role with limited permissions needs `cloudfront:TagResource` and `cloudfront:ListTagsForResource`.** The first deploy updates the tags on every site's and Router's CloudFront Functions and KV stores. Add both before you deploy.
- **A provider version pinned in `sst.config.ts` has to be at least** `aws` 7.48.0, `command` 1.2.1, `docker-build` 0.0.22, `random` 4.21.2 or `tls` 5.6.1. A lower pin stops with `You specified version <pin> of the "<provider>" provider. SST needs <version> or higher.` Raise the pin or remove it.
- **The first deploy after upgrading redeploys your containers.** Every image SST builds with docker-build is rebuilt once, so each `Service`, `Task` and container `Function` gets a new task definition revision and a rolling deployment. Your own `command.local.Command` and `remote.Command` resources run once more too.

### Fixes

- **`sst dev` no longer freezes when one of its clients stops reading.** A pane, a browser tab or another client that stopped reading events used to block the whole event bus, so every function invocation timed out until `sst dev` was restarted. That client now misses events instead, and the log file gets a warning. ([#27](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/27), [anomalyco/sst#7013](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/pull/7013))
- **`sst dev` no longer crashes with `concurrent map read and map write`** when many invocations arrive at once. ([#23](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/23), [anomalyco/sst#6970](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/pull/6970))
- **A new function URL or SSR site no longer fails to deploy now and then** with `ResourceConflictException: The function could not be updated due to a concurrent update operation`. The URL's permissions are now added after the URL exists. Existing stacks get the new ordering with no resource changes. ([#22](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/22), [anomalyco/sst#6933](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/pull/6933))
- **`ApiGatewayV2` with `cors: false` leaves the CORS configuration unset**, as its docs say. It used to set an empty one, under which API Gateway answers preflight requests itself and ignores the CORS headers your routes return. The next deploy removes the empty configuration from an existing API, in place. ([#26](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/26), [anomalyco/sst#6748](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/issues/6748))
- **`SsrSite` deploys to Auckland (`ap-southeast-6`).** The deploy crashed, because the region had no coordinates. ([#18](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/18), [anomalyco/sst#6792](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/pull/6792))

### Changes

- **Pulumi 3.267.0, and newer providers:** `@pulumi/aws` 7.48.0, `command` 1.2.1, `docker-build` 0.0.22, `random` 4.21.2 and `tls` 5.6.1. Cloudflare stays at 6.15.0, because from 6.18 the first deploy of an existing D1 database fails ([pulumi/pulumi-cloudflare#1583](https://github.com/pulumi/pulumi-cloudflare/issues/1583)). Vercel stays at 4.6.0. ([#18](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/18))
- **`Function` exposes its function URL resource as `nodes.url`**, when `url` is set. ([#22](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/22))
- Pulumi's log files and workspace file go to SST's folder instead of `~/.pulumi`. ([#18](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/18))

### Astro 6 and 7

SST's `astro-sst` 3.x can't build an Astro 6 or 7 app. The fork now publishes the adapter as [`@sst-community/astro-sst`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@sst-community/astro-sst) 4.0.0, which works with Astro 5.6 and later, 6 and 7. Install it under the old name so `import aws from "astro-sst"` keeps working:

```bash
npm install astro-sst@npm:@sst-community/astro-sst
```

- `sst init` installs it for a new Astro app.
- `sst.aws.Astro` stops before the build when an Astro 6 or 7 app still has SST's adapter, and names the `package.json` line to change.
- It fixes bugs from 3.1.4: cookies keep `Max-Age`, several cookies in stream mode arrive as separate headers, binary responses such as AVIF are no longer corrupted, trailing-slash redirects and `src/fetch.ts` work, and `Astro.clientAddress` can't be spoofed. The [adapter's changelog](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/blob/main/packages/astro-sst/CHANGELOG.md) has the full list, including what changes when you switch.
- Astro 5.0 to 5.5 need SST's 3.x, or an Astro upgrade.

([#47](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/47))

### Install

```bash
npm install sst@npm:@sst-community/sst@4.18.0
```

To switch an existing project, set its dependency to `"sst": "npm:@sst-community/sst@4.18.0"` and reinstall. Without Node:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sst-community/sst/main/install | bash
```
